q21097.en: The traffic light shown applies to scheduled passenger transport vehicles.

explain.short: Bars and a triangle instead of colours: this light is only for buses and trams on public lines (veicoli in servizio di linea).
explain.rule: This light is only for public buses and trams. Top horizontal bar = stop; yellow triangle = stop if you safely can; bottom vertical bar = go.
explain.trap: 'servizio di linea' (scheduled service) means buses and trams on fixed routes: correct.

sceneParams.caption: Light for public buses and trams
lines: For public buses and trams only

q21098.en: The traffic light shown makes scheduled passenger vehicles stop when the white bar at the top is lit.

explain.short: The horizontal white bar at the top works like a red light for buses and trams: they must stop.
explain.rule: This light is only for public buses and trams. Top horizontal bar = stop; yellow triangle = stop if you safely can; bottom vertical bar = go.
explain.trap: 'barra bianca in alto' (white bar at the top) is the horizontal bar: it means stop.

sceneParams.caption: Top horizontal bar = STOP

q21099.en: The traffic light shown lets public passenger transport vehicles go on when the white bar at the bottom is lit.

explain.short: The vertical white bar at the bottom works like green: buses and trams may go on.
explain.rule: This light is only for public buses and trams. Top horizontal bar = stop; yellow triangle = stop if you safely can; bottom vertical bar = go.
explain.trap: 'in basso' (at the bottom) is the vertical bar: it means go.

sceneParams.caption: Bottom vertical bar = GO

q21100.en: The traffic light shown is valid only for vehicles running on rails (trams, trains).

explain.short: It is for all scheduled public transport, buses too, not only for vehicles on rails.
explain.rule: This light is only for public buses and trams. Top horizontal bar = stop; yellow triangle = stop if you safely can; bottom vertical bar = go.
explain.trap: 'solo' (only) is the trap: buses on public lines use it too.

sceneParams.caption: Not only trams: public buses too
lines: For buses AND trams of public lines

q21101.en: The traffic light shown controls the passage of pedestrians.

explain.short: A pedestrian light shows a little walking man; this one has bars and a triangle for buses and trams.
explain.rule: This light is only for public buses and trams. Top horizontal bar = stop; yellow triangle = stop if you safely can; bottom vertical bar = go.
explain.trap: 'pedoni' (pedestrians) is wrong: there is no person symbol here.

sceneParams.caption: For buses and trams, not pedestrians
lines: No walking man: not for pedestrians

q21102.en: The traffic light shown indicates a level crossing without barriers.

explain.short: A level crossing without barriers has flashing red lights, not white bars and a yellow triangle.
explain.rule: This light is only for public buses and trams. Top horizontal bar = stop; yellow triangle = stop if you safely can; bottom vertical bar = go.
explain.trap: 'passaggio a livello' (level crossing) is wrong: this is a public transport light.

sceneParams.caption: Not a level crossing: a bus/tram light
lines: Level crossings use flashing red lights

q21103.en: The traffic light shown controls the passage on piers for boarding ferries.

explain.short: It has nothing to do with ferries: it tells buses and trams when to stop or go.
explain.rule: This light is only for public buses and trams. Top horizontal bar = stop; yellow triangle = stop if you safely can; bottom vertical bar = go.
explain.trap: 'pontili' (piers) and 'navi traghetto' (ferries) are invented.

sceneParams.caption: Not for ferries: for buses and trams

q21104.en: The traffic light shown indicates that a railway station is near.

explain.short: It does not announce a station; it tells buses and trams when to stop or go.
explain.rule: This light is only for public buses and trams. Top horizontal bar = stop; yellow triangle = stop if you safely can; bottom vertical bar = go.
explain.trap: 'stazione ferroviaria' (railway station) is invented.

sceneParams.caption: Not a station sign: a bus/tram light
lines: It does not warn of a station

q21105.en: The traffic light shown, with the yellow triangle lit, gives advance warning of roadworks.

explain.short: The yellow triangle works like a yellow light: stop, unless you are too close to stop safely.
explain.rule: This light is only for public buses and trams. Top horizontal bar = stop; yellow triangle = stop if you safely can; bottom vertical bar = go.
explain.trap: 'lavori in corso' (roadworks) is wrong: the triangle is the 'yellow' phase.

sceneParams.caption: Triangle = yellow phase, not roadworks
lines: Yellow triangle = like a yellow light

q21106.en: The traffic light shown controls pedestrians crossing at junctions.

explain.short: The walking-man symbols show that this light is for pedestrians crossing at junctions.
explain.rule: The walking-man light is for pedestrians. Green = cross; steady yellow = clear the crossing quickly; red = do not cross.
explain.trap: 'pedoni negli incroci' (pedestrians at junctions) is right.

sceneParams.caption: A light for pedestrians

q21107.en: The light signal shown is a pedestrian traffic light.

explain.short: Red, yellow and green walking men: it is the pedestrian light.
explain.rule: The walking-man light is for pedestrians. Green = cross; steady yellow = clear the crossing quickly; red = do not cross.
explain.trap: 'segnale luminoso' (light signal) is just another name for a traffic light: correct.

sceneParams.caption: Pedestrian traffic light

q21108.en: The traffic light shown, with the steady yellow light on, requires pedestrians already on the crossing to clear it quickly.

explain.short: Steady yellow tells pedestrians who are already crossing to hurry and reach the other side.
explain.rule: The walking-man light is for pedestrians. Green = cross; steady yellow = clear the crossing quickly; red = do not cross.
explain.trap: 'luce gialla fissa' (steady yellow) is for those already on the crossing: they clear it.

sceneParams.caption: Yellow: clear the crossing quickly

q21109.en: The traffic light shown, with the red light on, requires pedestrians not to cross.

explain.short: Red for pedestrians means the same as for cars: do not go, do not start crossing.
explain.rule: The walking-man light is for pedestrians. Green = cross; steady yellow = clear the crossing quickly; red = do not cross.
explain.trap: 'luce rossa' (red light) means stop: pedestrians must wait.

sceneParams.caption: Red: pedestrians must not cross
lines: Red walking man = do not cross

q21110.en: The light signal shown indicates that there is a school.

explain.short: It is a pedestrian traffic light: it tells pedestrians when to cross, it does not mark a school.
explain.rule: The walking-man light is for pedestrians. Green = cross; steady yellow = clear the crossing quickly; red = do not cross.
explain.trap: 'scuola' (school) is invented: schools have a danger sign with children.

sceneParams.caption: A pedestrian light, not a school sign

q21111.en: The traffic light shown indicates that a running race is taking place.

explain.short: It is a normal pedestrian light; it says nothing about races.
explain.rule: The walking-man light is for pedestrians. Green = cross; steady yellow = clear the crossing quickly; red = do not cross.
explain.trap: 'gara podistica' (running race) is invented.

sceneParams.caption: A pedestrian light, not a race

q21112.en: In motorway service areas the traffic light shown indicates pedestrian underpasses.

explain.short: It is a pedestrian light for crossings and junctions; it does not point to underpasses.
explain.rule: The walking-man light is for pedestrians. Green = cross; steady yellow = clear the crossing quickly; red = do not cross.
explain.trap: 'sottopassaggi pedonali' (pedestrian underpasses) is invented.

sceneParams.caption: A pedestrian light, not an underpass

q21113.en: The traffic light shown is at the entrance of the underground (metro).

explain.short: It is a pedestrian light at road crossings, not a sign for the metro.
explain.rule: The walking-man light is for pedestrians. Green = cross; steady yellow = clear the crossing quickly; red = do not cross.
explain.trap: 'metropolitana' (underground) is invented.

sceneParams.caption: A pedestrian light, not the metro

q21114.en: The traffic light shown indicates boarding gates in port areas.

explain.short: It is a pedestrian light; it has nothing to do with ports or boarding.
explain.rule: The walking-man light is for pedestrians. Green = cross; steady yellow = clear the crossing quickly; red = do not cross.
explain.trap: 'cancelli di imbarco' (boarding gates) is invented.

sceneParams.caption: A pedestrian light, not a port gate

q21115.en: The traffic light shown indicates the entrance of a sports venue.

explain.short: It is a pedestrian light; it does not show where a sports venue is.
explain.rule: The walking-man light is for pedestrians. Green = cross; steady yellow = clear the crossing quickly; red = do not cross.
explain.trap: 'struttura sportiva' (sports venue) is invented.

sceneParams.caption: A pedestrian light, not a sports venue

q21116.en: The traffic light shown is at the end of a cycle path, to control crossing the road.

explain.short: Bicycle lights are typically placed where a cycle path (pista ciclabile) meets the road, so cyclists cross safely.
explain.rule: The bicycle light is only for cyclists, often at the end of a cycle path. Green = cross; steady yellow = clear the junction quickly; red = stop.
explain.trap: 'uscita di una pista ciclabile' (end of a cycle path) is right.

sceneParams.caption: Bike light where the cycle path ends
lines: At the end of a cycle path

q21117.en: The light signal shown is a traffic light reserved for cyclists.

explain.short: The bicycle symbols show that only cyclists must follow this light.
explain.rule: The bicycle light is only for cyclists, often at the end of a cycle path. Green = cross; steady yellow = clear the junction quickly; red = stop.
explain.trap: 'riservato' (reserved) is right: only bicycles.

sceneParams.caption: Light reserved for cyclists

q21118.en: The traffic light shown, with the red light on, makes bicycles stop.

explain.short: Red on a bike light means stop, just like red for cars.
explain.rule: The bicycle light is only for cyclists, often at the end of a cycle path. Green = cross; steady yellow = clear the junction quickly; red = stop.
explain.trap: 'luce rossa' (red light) = stop: correct.

sceneParams.caption: Red bike = cyclists stop

q21119.en: The traffic light shown, with the steady yellow light on, requires cyclists who have already entered the junction to clear it quickly.

explain.short: Steady yellow tells cyclists already in the junction to leave it quickly; the others stop.
explain.rule: The bicycle light is only for cyclists, often at the end of a cycle path. Green = cross; steady yellow = clear the junction quickly; red = stop.
explain.trap: 'se lo hanno già impegnato' (if already in it) is the key: they clear it fast.

sceneParams.caption: Yellow bike: clear the junction fast

q21120.en: The traffic light shown, with the green light on, lets only cyclists cross the junction.

explain.short: The light is reserved for bicycles, so its green is a go only for cyclists.
explain.rule: The bicycle light is only for cyclists, often at the end of a cycle path. Green = cross; steady yellow = clear the junction quickly; red = stop.
explain.trap: 'soltanto' (only) is correct here: the light is for cyclists alone.

sceneParams.caption: Green bike: only cyclists go

q21121.en: The traffic light shown indicates a lane reserved for bicycles and mopeds.

explain.short: It is a traffic light for cyclists only; it does not mark a lane, and mopeds do not follow it.
explain.rule: The bicycle light is only for cyclists, often at the end of a cycle path. Green = cross; steady yellow = clear the junction quickly; red = stop.
explain.trap: 'ciclomotori' (mopeds) is the trap: the light is for bicycles only.

sceneParams.caption: Bikes only: not a lane, not mopeds
lines: Not a lane, and not for mopeds

q21122.en: The traffic light shown indicates that a cycle race is taking place.

explain.short: It is a normal traffic light for cyclists; it says nothing about races.
explain.rule: The bicycle light is only for cyclists, often at the end of a cycle path. Green = cross; steady yellow = clear the junction quickly; red = stop.
explain.trap: 'gara ciclistica' (cycle race) is invented.

sceneParams.caption: A bike light, not a race

q21123.en: The traffic light shown indicates that work to build a cycle path is in progress.

explain.short: It is a light for cyclists; roadworks have their own danger sign.
explain.rule: The bicycle light is only for cyclists, often at the end of a cycle path. Green = cross; steady yellow = clear the junction quickly; red = stop.
explain.trap: 'lavori in corso' (works in progress) is invented.

sceneParams.caption: A bike light, not roadworks

q21124.en: The traffic light shown indicates a lane reserved for motorcycles.

explain.short: The symbol is a bicycle, not a motorbike, and it is a traffic light, not a lane sign.
explain.rule: The bicycle light is only for cyclists, often at the end of a cycle path. Green = cross; steady yellow = clear the junction quickly; red = stop.
explain.trap: 'motocicli' (motorcycles) is wrong: it is for bicycles.

sceneParams.caption: Bicycles, not motorcycles

q21125.en: The traffic light shown indicates that bicycles are not allowed through.

explain.short: It is not a ban: it tells cyclists when to stop and when they may go.
explain.rule: The bicycle light is only for cyclists, often at the end of a cycle path. Green = cross; steady yellow = clear the junction quickly; red = stop.
explain.trap: 'divieto di transito' (no entry) is wrong: a ban is a round sign, not a light.

sceneParams.caption: Not a ban: tells cyclists when to go

q21126.en: The traffic light shown applies to all two-wheeled vehicles.

explain.short: It is only for bicycles; mopeds and motorbikes follow the normal vehicle lights.
explain.rule: The bicycle light is only for cyclists, often at the end of a cycle path. Green = cross; steady yellow = clear the junction quickly; red = stop.
explain.trap: 'tutti i veicoli a due ruote' (all two-wheelers) is too wide: only bicycles.

sceneParams.caption: Bicycles only, not all two-wheelers
lines: Only bicycles, not mopeds or motorbikes

keywords.it: tutti i veicoli a due ruote

q21127.en: The flashing yellow light, of type B or C in the figure, is placed next to the vehicle traffic light.

explain.short: B and C sit beside the normal traffic light for vehicles, to warn drivers who turn right.
explain.rule: Flashing yellow = go with care. B (walking man) and C (bicycle) sit next to the car light: turning right, give way to pedestrians (B) or cyclists (C).
explain.trap: 'affiancata' (placed beside) is right: next to the vehicle light.

sceneParams.caption: B and C sit beside the car traffic light
lines: B and C: next to the vehicle light

q21128.en: The flashing yellow light, of type C in the figure, indicates that vehicles turning right must give way to bicycles.

explain.short: C shows a bicycle: when you turn right, give way to cyclists crossing the road you enter.
explain.rule: Flashing yellow = go with care. B (walking man) and C (bicycle) sit next to the car light: turning right, give way to pedestrians (B) or cyclists (C).
explain.trap: 'tipo C' is the bicycle: give way to bikes.

sceneParams.caption: C: turning right, give way to bikes

q21129.en: The flashing yellow light, of type B in the figure, indicates that when turning right vehicles must give way to pedestrians.

explain.short: B shows a walking man: when you turn right, give way to pedestrians crossing the road you enter.
explain.rule: Flashing yellow = go with care. B (walking man) and C (bicycle) sit next to the car light: turning right, give way to pedestrians (B) or cyclists (C).
explain.trap: 'tipo B' is the walking man: give way to pedestrians.

sceneParams.caption: B: turning right, give way to pedestrians
lines: B (walking man): turning right, give way

q21131.en: The flashing yellow light, of type C in the figure, indicates a lane reserved for all two-wheeled vehicles.

explain.short: C is a warning light: turning right, give way to cyclists. It does not mark any lane.
explain.rule: Flashing yellow = go with care. B (walking man) and C (bicycle) sit next to the car light: turning right, give way to pedestrians (B) or cyclists (C).
explain.trap: 'corsia riservata' (reserved lane) is wrong: lights warn, they do not mark lanes.

sceneParams.caption: C warns of cyclists; it is not a lane
lines: C = give way to bikes, not a lane

q21132.en: The flashing yellow light, of type B in the figure, indicates a pedestrian avenue.

explain.short: B warns drivers turning right to give way to crossing pedestrians; it does not mark a pedestrian street.
explain.rule: Flashing yellow = go with care. B (walking man) and C (bicycle) sit next to the car light: turning right, give way to pedestrians (B) or cyclists (C).
explain.trap: 'viale pedonale' (pedestrian avenue) is invented.

sceneParams.caption: B warns of pedestrians crossing

q21133.en: The flashing yellow light, of type A in the figure, is a traffic light for scheduled passenger transport vehicles.

explain.short: A is a plain flashing yellow: it tells all drivers to go on with care. The bus and tram light has white bars.
explain.rule: Flashing yellow = go with care. B (walking man) and C (bicycle) sit next to the car light: turning right, give way to pedestrians (B) or cyclists (C).
explain.trap: 'servizio di linea' (scheduled transport) is wrong for A: A is a general warning.

sceneParams.caption: A = go with care, not a bus light
lines: A (plain) = go with care, give way

q21134.en: The flashing yellow light, of type C in the figure, indicates a lane reserved for mopeds.

explain.short: C shows a bicycle and warns to give way to cyclists when turning right; it marks no lane and is not about mopeds.
explain.rule: Flashing yellow = go with care. B (walking man) and C (bicycle) sit next to the car light: turning right, give way to pedestrians (B) or cyclists (C).
explain.trap: 'ciclomotori' (mopeds) is wrong: the symbol is a bicycle.

sceneParams.caption: C warns of bicycles, not a moped lane

q21135.en: The light signals shown are green-wave traffic lights.

explain.short: Numbers 50, 40, 30 inside the lights: this is the green-wave light (onda verde).
explain.rule: The green-wave light shows one advised speed at a time, to catch the next lights green. It is advice only, on roads with timed lights.
explain.trap: 'onda verde' (green wave) is the right name.

sceneParams.caption: Green-wave light

q21136.en: The traffic light shown advises the speed to keep, so as to find the green light at the next traffic light.

explain.short: The lit number is the speed that lets you arrive at the next lights when they are green.
explain.rule: The green-wave light shows one advised speed at a time, to catch the next lights green. It is advice only, on roads with timed lights.
explain.trap: 'consiglia' (advises) is right: it is advice, not an order.

sceneParams.caption: Advised speed to catch the next green

q21137.en: The green-wave light shown is found on roads with several junctions where the traffic lights are synchronised (timed).

explain.short: A green wave only works where many traffic lights in a row are timed together.
explain.rule: The green-wave light shows one advised speed at a time, to catch the next lights green. It is advice only, on roads with timed lights.
explain.trap: 'sincronizzati' (synchronised) is right: the lights are timed in sequence.

sceneParams.caption: Roads with many timed traffic lights
lines: Many synchronised lights in a row

q21138.en: The traffic light shown signals the recommended speed for taking advantage of the green wave.

explain.short: The lit number is the recommended speed: keep it and you meet green lights one after another.
explain.rule: The green-wave light shows one advised speed at a time, to catch the next lights green. It is advice only, on roads with timed lights.
explain.trap: 'velocità consigliata' (recommended speed) is right.

sceneParams.caption: Recommended speed for the green wave

q21139.en: Of the three lights of the traffic light shown, only one comes on, while the others are off.

explain.short: Only one speed is advised at a time, so only one number is lit.
explain.rule: The green-wave light shows one advised speed at a time, to catch the next lights green. It is advice only, on roads with timed lights.
explain.trap: 'soltanto una' (only one) is right: one number at a time.

sceneParams.caption: Only one number lit at a time
lines: One number lit, the others off

q21140.en: The traffic light shown obliges you to keep the speed indicated.

explain.short: The green-wave speed is only advice; you are not obliged to keep it.
explain.rule: The green-wave light shows one advised speed at a time, to catch the next lights green. It is advice only, on roads with timed lights.
explain.trap: 'obbliga' (obliges) is the trap: it only advises.

sceneParams.caption: Advice, not an obligation

q21141.en: The traffic light shown does not allow you to exceed the speed indicated.

explain.short: The number is an advised speed, not a speed limit; the road's normal limit still applies.
explain.rule: The green-wave light shows one advised speed at a time, to catch the next lights green. It is advice only, on roads with timed lights.
explain.trap: 'non consente di superare' (does not allow exceeding) makes it a limit: wrong.

sceneParams.caption: Advised speed, not a speed limit

q21142.en: The traffic light shown requires the driver to keep the distance indicated from the vehicle in front.

explain.short: The numbers are speeds in km/h, not distances, and they are only advice.
explain.rule: The green-wave light shows one advised speed at a time, to catch the next lights green. It is advice only, on roads with timed lights.
explain.trap: 'distanza' (distance) is wrong: the numbers are speeds.

sceneParams.caption: Speeds, not distances

q21143.en: The traffic light shown tells you to go on with caution.

explain.short: It does not warn of danger: it advises the speed to catch the next green light.
explain.rule: The green-wave light shows one advised speed at a time, to catch the next lights green. It is advice only, on roads with timed lights.
explain.trap: 'procedere con prudenza' (go with caution) is the meaning of flashing yellow, not of this light.

sceneParams.caption: It advises a speed, not caution

q21144.en: The traffic light shown, even when off, indicates the compulsory speed.

explain.short: A switched-off light says nothing, and even when lit the speed is only advised.
explain.rule: The green-wave light shows one advised speed at a time, to catch the next lights green. It is advice only, on roads with timed lights.
explain.trap: 'anche se spento' (even if off) and 'obbligatoria' (compulsory) are both wrong.

sceneParams.caption: Off = no message; lit = advice only

q21145.en: The green-wave light shown is also placed on motorways.

explain.short: Motorways have no traffic lights at junctions, so a green wave makes no sense there.
explain.rule: The green-wave light shows one advised speed at a time, to catch the next lights green. It is advice only, on roads with timed lights.
explain.trap: 'anche sulle autostrade' (also on motorways) is the trap: only roads with timed lights.

sceneParams.caption: Not on motorways: no traffic lights there

q21146.en: The green-wave light shown gives the maximum speed limits for cars, motorcycles and lorries.

explain.short: The numbers are advised speeds for everyone, not maximum limits for each type of vehicle.
explain.rule: The green-wave light shows one advised speed at a time, to catch the next lights green. It is advice only, on roads with timed lights.
explain.trap: 'limiti massimi' (maximum limits) is wrong: it only advises.

sceneParams.caption: Advised speeds, not maximum limits
lines: Not limits for cars, bikes, lorries

q21147.en: The green-wave light shown indicates the speeds that some vehicles must compulsorily respect.

explain.short: The speed is advice for all drivers; it is compulsory for nobody.
explain.rule: The green-wave light shows one advised speed at a time, to catch the next lights green. It is advice only, on roads with timed lights.
explain.trap: 'obbligatoriamente' (compulsorily) is the trap: never compulsory.

sceneParams.caption: Advice for all, compulsory for none

q21148.en: The green-wave light shown is a traffic light for roadworks.

explain.short: It advises a speed to catch green lights; it has nothing to do with roadworks.
explain.rule: The green-wave light shows one advised speed at a time, to catch the next lights green. It is advice only, on roads with timed lights.
explain.trap: 'lavori in corso' (roadworks) is invented.

sceneParams.caption: Green wave, not roadworks

q21149.en: The green-wave light shown indicates the distance from motorway toll booths.

explain.short: The numbers are speeds, not distances, and green waves are not on motorways.
explain.rule: The green-wave light shows one advised speed at a time, to catch the next lights green. It is advice only, on roads with timed lights.
explain.trap: 'caselli autostradali' (motorway toll booths) is invented.

sceneParams.caption: Speeds, not distance to toll booths

q21150.en: The reversible-lane traffic light shown is placed on a carriageway with at least three lanes.

explain.short: Reversible lanes need at least three lanes, so the middle ones can change direction.
explain.rule: Reversible-lane lights hang over each lane (at least 3 lanes). Green arrow = lane open; red X = lane closed; flashing yellow arrow = move to the lane shown.
explain.trap: 'almeno tre corsie' (at least three lanes) is right.

sceneParams.caption: At least three lanes

q21151.en: The reversible-lane traffic light shown allows traffic in the lane indicated by the green arrow.

explain.short: A green arrow pointing down over a lane means that lane is open to you.
explain.rule: Reversible-lane lights hang over each lane (at least 3 lanes). Green arrow = lane open; red X = lane closed; flashing yellow arrow = move to the lane shown.
explain.trap: 'freccia verde' (green arrow) = you may drive in that lane.

sceneParams.caption: Green arrow = lane open

q21152.en: The reversible-lane traffic light shown, with a flashing yellow arrow, requires the driver to leave that lane and move to the one indicated.

explain.short: The flashing yellow diagonal arrow tells you the lane is about to close: move to the lane it points to.
explain.rule: Reversible-lane lights hang over each lane (at least 3 lanes). Green arrow = lane open; red X = lane closed; flashing yellow arrow = move to the lane shown.
explain.trap: 'freccia gialla lampeggiante' (flashing yellow arrow) = change lane.

sceneParams.caption: Flashing yellow arrow = move over

q21153.en: The reversible-lane traffic light shown indicates the lane for slow vehicles.

explain.short: It shows which lanes are open or closed in your direction; it is not about slow vehicles.
explain.rule: Reversible-lane lights hang over each lane (at least 3 lanes). Green arrow = lane open; red X = lane closed; flashing yellow arrow = move to the lane shown.
explain.trap: 'veicoli lenti' (slow vehicles) is invented.

sceneParams.caption: Open/closed lanes, not a slow lane

q21154.en: The reversible-lane traffic light shown indicates the lane for emergency stops.

explain.short: It tells you which lanes you may drive in; it does not mark an emergency lane.
explain.rule: Reversible-lane lights hang over each lane (at least 3 lanes). Green arrow = lane open; red X = lane closed; flashing yellow arrow = move to the lane shown.
explain.trap: 'sosta di emergenza' (emergency stop) is invented.

sceneParams.caption: Open/closed lanes, not emergency stops

q21155.en: The reversible-lane traffic light shown indicates the lane reserved for overtaking.

explain.short: It shows which lanes are open in your direction; it does not reserve a lane for overtaking.
explain.rule: Reversible-lane lights hang over each lane (at least 3 lanes). Green arrow = lane open; red X = lane closed; flashing yellow arrow = move to the lane shown.
explain.trap: 'riservata al sorpasso' (reserved for overtaking) is invented.

sceneParams.caption: Open/closed lanes, not an overtaking lane

q21156.en: The reversible-lane traffic light shown is placed only on one-way carriageways.

explain.short: Reversible lanes change direction, so they are used on two-way carriageways, not only one-way ones.
explain.rule: Reversible-lane lights hang over each lane (at least 3 lanes). Green arrow = lane open; red X = lane closed; flashing yellow arrow = move to the lane shown.
explain.trap: 'solo' (only) and 'senso unico' (one-way) are the trap.

sceneParams.caption: Used on two-way roads, not only one-way
